title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 8
paragraphs: So the Scythians speak of themselves and of the region above them. But the Hellenes who dwell around the Pontus say the following. Heracles, driving the cattle of Geryones, came to this land, then desert, which the Scythians now inhabit; and Geryones, the tale says, dwelt away from the Pontic region, living in the island called by the Hellenes Erytheia, near Gadeira outside the Pillars of Heracles by the Ocean. As to the Ocean, they say indeed that it flows around the whole earth, beginning from the place of the sunrising, but they do not prove this by facts. From there Heracles came to the land now called Scythia, and since a storm came upon him together with icy cold, he drew his lion's skin over him and went to sleep. Meanwhile the mares harnessed to his chariot, as they were grazing, vanished by some miraculous chance.
